ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: Across Q3, the account is overwhelmingly constrained by budget caps, not rank: most in-scope campaigns run at ~99.9% budget utilization with 79–83% impression share lost to budget and 0% lost to rank at the campaign level. The biggest incremental volume sits in Shopping (Apparel/Electronics/Home & Garden) and Non-Brand Seasonal, which collectively show very low search impression share (17–21%) driven by budget loss. Secondary issues: a few high-quality keywords are losing share to rank (81%/79% rank loss) indicating selective bid/rank gaps at the keyword layer, and Non-Brand Seasonal has negative-keyword conflicts blocking ~6,940 impressions (including 5,200 blocked on “free shipping promo code”). Competitor-brand leakage is material in impression volume (2,058 zero-click impressions; 56.1% of competitor-term impressions), but no competitor-brand terms are converting, so that inventory is mostly waste/drag rather than growth.
notable_patterns: Budget loss dominates opportunity in the campaigns that drive missed impressions: Shopping - Apparel (18% IS; 82% lost to budget; 99.9% budget utilization; 76,752 missed imps), Shopping - Electronics (17% IS; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization; 69,056 missed imps), Shopping - Home & Garden (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization; 50,544 missed imps), and Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo (21% IS; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization; 57,512 missed imps).

Brand Search is the exception: 60% IS with 40% lost to budget and only 75.4% budget utilization, plus very strong ROAS (24.26 on €494.34 spend), implying the constraint there is not daily caps but likely coverage/targeting (or budget scheduling) rather than rank (0% lost to rank).

Keyword layer shows pockets of rank loss despite campaign-level 0% rank loss: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) has 19% IS with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) has 21% IS with 79% lost to rank—these are prime candidates for bid/rank tuning once budget headroom is created.

Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo is self-blocking demand: 3 negative conflicts block an estimated 6,940 impressions (including negative “free” blocking “free shipping promo code” for 5,200 imps), and the same area also contains low-QS waste (“free shipping promo code” QS 3.5; €24.18 spend; €60.45 CPA; plus “deals near me today” QS 2.5 with spend €15.39 and no tracked conversions).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Very low reach (18% impression share) is being throttled by budget (82% lost to budget) while the campaign is essentially fully capped (99.9% budget utilization). With 76,752 missed impressions, this is one of the largest scalable pools in the account; performance is acceptable but not standout (ROAS 3.33).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget only if you can simultaneously tighten product/priority structure (exclude low-margin SKUs, split top sellers) so incremental spend maintains ~3.3+ ROAS; otherwise reallocate budget from lower-ROAS channels into this campaign first due to the 82% budget loss and large missed-impression volume.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Reach is capped by budget (17% IS; 83% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with a large missed-impression pool (69,056). ROAS is 3.29, so scaling is possible but should be controlled via product segmentation and profitability rules.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Reallocate/increase budget while segmenting by margin/price band; prioritize electronics SKUs that already convert, and constrain exposure on low-margin categories to protect ROAS as volume increases.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Budget-limited (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with 50,544 missed impressions, but this category has the best Shopping ROAS in the set (4.34). This is the cleanest place to scale profitably.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize incremental budget here first among Shopping campaigns, because it combines heavy budget loss (81%) with comparatively strong ROAS (4.34), indicating the highest likelihood of efficient incremental conversions.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: The campaign is hard budget-capped (99.9% utilization; 79% lost to budget; 21% IS) and also has self-inflicted coverage loss from negatives (6,940 blocked impressions). Despite a strong avg quality score (8.8) and decent ROAS (3.88), it’s not capturing demand it’s eligible for.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Fix negative keyword conflicts first (recover the blocked 6,940 impressions), then add budget to relieve the 79% budget-loss ceiling; simultaneously prune/contain low-QS, non-converting queries to keep marginal efficiency stable.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Severely budget-limited (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with 54,756 missed impressions and ROAS 4.91 on small spend (€98.70). This suggests untapped scalable demand if conversion tracking/value is reliable.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget cautiously in steps while verifying that incremental spend maintains ROAS near ~4.9; if it holds, this is a strong candidate to absorb reallocated budget from weaker areas.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate/increase budgets in the highest missed-impression pools (Shopping + Seasonal + Full Catalog)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Five campaigns are effectively capped (~99.9% budget utilization) and are losing the majority of eligible impressions to budget: Shopping - Apparel (82% lost; 76,752 missed imps), Shopping - Electronics (83%; 69,056), Shopping - Home & Garden (81%; 50,544), Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo (79%; 57,512), and Performance Max - Full Catalog (81%; 54,756). Campaign-level lost-to-rank is 0% across the board, so budget is the binding constraint at the campaign layer.
recommended_steps: Shift incremental budget first to the best efficiency among the capped set (e.g., Shopping - Home & Garden ROAS 4.34; Full Catalog ROAS 4.91) before scaling lower-ROAS capped campaigns (Apparel 3.33; Electronics 3.29).
Increase budgets in 15–25% steps (per campaign) and hold for a full learning/attribution cycle; continue until lost-to-budget meaningfully drops from ~80% toward <40–50%.
If total budget is fixed, fund the increases by trimming spend where it is least proven (e.g., low-QS non-brand waste noted in search terms/keywords) rather than touching Brand Search (ROAS 24.26).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to budget on the scaled campaigns: move from ~79–83% toward <50% while holding ROAS at or above current levels (≈3.3+ for Shopping, ≈3.9+ for Seasonal, ≈4.9 for Full Catalog).

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve negative keyword conflicts that are blocking eligible Non-Brand Seasonal demand
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3 conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions inside Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo—most notably negative “free” blocking the keyword “free shipping promo code” (5,200 blocked imps), plus “DIY” blocking “kitchen appliances clearance DIY install” (980) and “returns” blocking “winter jacket sale returns policy” (760). This is recoverable coverage on top of the campaign’s existing 79% lost to budget.
recommended_steps: Edit negatives to avoid blocking intended intent: convert broad negatives like “free” into more precise negatives (or add exceptions via exact-match negatives) so promotional queries you actually want can serve.

For “returns” and “DIY,” decide intent: if you don’t want service/how-to traffic, keep negatives but add alternative keywords/ad groups for high-intent transactional variants; if you do want it, narrow the negatives to only the irrelevant patterns.
After changes, re-check blocked-impression estimates and search-term logs for 7 days to ensure the conflicts are resolved without reopening irrelevant traffic.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Recovered impressions and clicks in Non-Brand Seasonal (expect measurable lift vs. baseline given 6,940 previously blocked impressions), with CPA not degrading from current levels (campaign ROAS ~3.88 as a guardrail).

recommendation_cards.title: Fix selective rank loss on high-quality seasonal keywords (bid/rank tuning)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Despite campaign-level 0% lost to rank, the keyword sample shows high-QS terms with severe rank loss: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5) has 19% IS with 81% lost to rank; “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0) has 21% IS with 79% lost to rank; even brand-adjacent “pilot account promo code” (QS 9.5) shows 42% lost to rank at 58% IS. These are the exact terms where small bid changes can unlock disproportionately more top coverage.
recommended_steps: Increase bids (or loosen bid limits) specifically on the high-QS/high-rank-loss terms and keep changes isolated to their ad groups to avoid broad CPC inflation.
If you’re using query matching beyond exact, split these into tighter ad groups with copy aligned to the term to preserve QS while improving rank.
Reassess after 3–5 days: keep increases only if incremental conversions/revenue scale proportionally.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share lost to rank on those keywords: target a reduction from ~79–81% down toward <40–50% without CPC spikes that erase ROAS.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage (no conversions)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand queries generated 2,058 zero-click impressions, and 56.1% of competitor-term impressions come from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”, “ionian goods co”, “acropolis retail quote”). There are zero competitor-brand terms that convert in the provided sample.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand names (and close variants) as phrase/exact negatives in non-brand search and any catch-all query sources where they can trigger.
Keep an exception list only if you have a deliberate conquesting strategy and a separate budget with conversion goals; otherwise block broadly.
Re-check search-term logs after 1 week to confirm competitor-brand impression volume and spend drop without impacting non-brand converting terms.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions/spend from competitor-brand terms: drive the 56.1% zero-click competitor-term share down materially (aim <10%) and monitor overall non-brand conversion volume for unintended suppression.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut/contain low-quality, inefficient non-brand keywords before scaling spend further
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several keywords show low quality scores with spend that is not paying back: “free shipping promo code” (QS 3.5; €24.18 spend; €60.45 cost/conv), “deals near me today” (QS 2.5; €15.39 spend; no conversions recorded), and “kitchen appliances clearance” (QS 3.0; €9.60 spend; €96.00 cost/conv). This mix will dilute results as you raise budgets to relieve the ~80% budget loss.
recommended_steps: Move these terms into a separate, tightly capped ad group/campaign (or pause) so they don’t compete with efficient seasonal/product terms for limited budget.
Add intent-shaping negatives around ‘near me today’ type queries if you can’t serve local intent; tighten matching to focus on transactional modifiers.
Rewrite ads/landing alignment only if you keep them; otherwise remove and redeploy budget to higher-return queries/campaigns.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Account-level CPA/ROAS stability while budgets rise: expect improvement if low-QS waste is removed (watch QS distribution and cost/conv on non-brand).

already_working: Ad creative coverage is not a bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good).

Auction competitiveness is generally fine (not screaming rank crisis): avg outranking share is 52.9% and self top-of-page rate is 49.6% vs competitors’ 42.4%, suggesting you’re not systematically losing auctions when eligible.

Brand Search is highly efficient (ROAS 24.26 on €494.34 spend) and shows 0% impression share lost to rank; it doesn’t need aggressive structural changes—keep it protected while you scale capped non-brand/shopping demand.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: You’re materially under-capturing eligible Retail search demand primarily because budgets are binding (not ad rank): the account’s impression share is well below the Retail benchmark while nearly four-fifths of eligible impressions are being lost to budget. At the same time, the broader market is getting more competitive this quarter in your market (search spend is growing QoQ), which increases the opportunity cost of staying budget-capped—missed auctions today are more likely to be captured by competitors as spend rises. Acting now (1) converts existing eligibility into incremental volume by reducing budget loss, and (2) protects share as competition intensifies.

email_copy.subject: EUR 12,644 upside—your account is capped, not outbid
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t losing because you’re getting outranked—it’s mostly not getting into the auction long enough to compete. In Q3, the patterns are consistent: when you’re eligible, you show; you’re just budget-capped before demand runs out.
why_now_bullets: Retail competition is rising (search spend growth QoQ is 9.0%), while your account is only capturing 21.29% impression share vs the vertical benchmark of 35.0%.
The account is losing 78.7% of eligible impressions to budget while losing only 0.0% to rank—this is a budget access problem, not an ad position problem.
With a daily budget of EUR 420, you’re effectively choosing which auctions to skip—right as competitors are leaning in with higher spend.
email_copy.stat_sub: Estimated upside available without a full rebuild
email_copy.impact_line: We sized EUR 12,644 of incremental revenue primarily from removing budget friction in the campaigns that are already trying to spend (and cleaning up a few preventable blockers). The key point: you don’t need to “fix rank” broadly—your account is already competitive when it can enter the auction; it just runs out of room too early.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-by-campaign view of where the upside is concentrated, so it’s clear where budget and cleanup work will actually pay back.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the short list of moves that unlock more eligible volume first (budget + coverage), then tighten efficiency so the extra spend doesn’t leak.
email_copy.working_intro: A few fundamentals are already in good shape—so scaling doesn’t require starting over, just removing the constraints.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we lift impression share from 21.29% toward 35.0% while keeping today’s click rate assumption (the cautious version), the numbers below show what that translates to in additional volume—and it’s the path to capturing that EUR 12,644.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map the exact first 7-day plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “Tue” or “Thu” and I’ll send two specific time options for a 15-minute walkthrough. If you’d rather skip the call, reply “plan” and I’ll email the 3-step rollout order (what to change first, what to hold, what to monitor).
email_copy.ps: P.S. The fastest win is removing the self-inflicted blockers (coverage that’s currently prevented from serving) before adding budget—so every extra euro goes into auctions that can actually convert.
